annotations.title: Check whether chips work together (draft wiring)

description: Will these chips work together? Ask before you have a netlist. Reads ONLY the extraction jobs you pass (2-12, from your account; repeats are removed, and two runs of one part are one part), drafts a starting wiring from pin names the way the DatasheetVend Workbench does (one elected microcontroller wired to each device over I2C or SPI), runs the electrical rules on it and answers per pair. The answer rests on that DRAFT wiring, never on your schematic: `basis` is 'draft_wiring', and to audit a real board use datasheetvend_crosscheck_netlist. Never a bare 'yes': each pair is CONFLICT, NO CONFLICT FOUND (nothing the bench could check failed, not 'they work together') or NOT CHECKED, with checks_ran of checks_total and what is missing. Device-to-device pairs are never wired, so they stay NOT CHECKED; with no part proven a microcontroller nothing is wired at all; UART and CAN are never drafted. Read the pair counts (conflict_pairs, no_conflict_pairs, not_checked_pairs), `verdict`, `rule_coverage` and the assumed-value counts before you repeat an answer. Findings are capped, with their total. A job whose outputs are gone is refused. Deterministic: runs DatasheetVend's checks in code, calls no model and extracts nothing. Costs no credits. Needs a DatasheetVend API key.

job_ids.description: 2-12 extraction jobs in your account, one or more per part. Include each part's pinout and logic_levels runs.

protocol.description: Which bus the draft wires: AUTO (default) lets the bench choose per device, as the Workbench does.
